title: I lost an ESP32
content: Somewhere between cleaning my desk at work and arranging monitors, one of my ESP32 boards disappeared.
I looked everywhere. Nothing.
The ESP32 has officially entered another dimension.
And the worst thing is that it was one of the new ESP32 S3 and it has been already uploaded with Monbit version!
I just realised that I noticed it is gone on Monday. Since then, nothing new.

title: I found the ESP32!
content: The ESP32 miraculously emerged from the another dimension - it was under one of the monitor!
I was very surprised. I moved my monitor a bit to adjust its postition and then I noticed there is something under it. What a pleasant surprise when I took it out and it was the ESP!
Of course I was looking everywhere at desk and I assumed it fell into the bin but no. It was under the monitor the whole time.
Silly me...

title: What I am working on
content: Right now I am focusing on my studies, again, so there has not been much time to work on my ongoing projects.
But when I have some time, I am working on a simple Attendance app. I won't be posting it as a separate project because I am building it mostly with Claude.
It's not a project which I really want to do, it just happens to be quite a necassary because I am moving in December to new City and I will be mostly working remotely.
Thus I have decided to 'build' this, so I can have a nice overview of my working hours, holidays, overtimes etc + I can export it to Excel and send it to HR so they know my work hours.
It's not anything fancy, just a simple project and once again I don't want to take the credit for it, because I heavily used AI for it.
It has one benefit though. It took me about one week to finish and I was 'working on it' only for one weekend + few hours during the week.
I have decided that I want to use Vercel for 'hosting' it and Supabase as database entry because I want it to be accesible to more users if needed and I don't want to pay for another domain
Bellow are some screenshots of it and you can check the blob on my git: https://github.com/Jim-23/attendance-app

title: What I am working on
content: I am still trying to study whenever I have free time, and then I usually spend the rest of the evening playing some games and talking to my friends on Discord. (Yes, I have friends! xD). There isn't much time for personal projects, and there won't be until February because I have my exams during the last week of January 2027.

On top of that, I am moving out this Saturday, so there is some packing to do. This also means that I am starting to work remotely next week, with commuting to work probably twice that week. I am kinda scared of it because the total travel time is around 2 hours, so that would be 4 hours of travelling + 8.5 hours of work. The rest of the time is for other stuff and sleeping, which isn't much.

On another note, I am a big fan of e-ink displays, and since I recently sold my Boox Palma 1, I was on the hunt for a new e-reader. I wanted something light, not Android-based, with physical buttons (a plus), and ideally something cheap with a colour display.

Of course, I did a lot of research, watched tons of comparison videos, and the only one that met my criteria was the PocketBook Verse Pro Color (the price was the main thing that made me consider it, and I also like that it's from Europe). After purchasing and trying it, I had to return it. I was very disappointed with the system speed (even with the Koreader installed). I liked the size and buttons, but that's probably it. I also encountered a few unexpected restarts while reading and battery drainage overnight. The software seems not to be optimised very well at all. So here I am, hunting again.

So the research continues. There weren't many options left. There was the Kobo Clara Colour, Kindle (they just released the 2026 Colorsoft version), and a few other brands. Now I am very happy that I went with Kobo!

Kobo is smooth (compared to PocketBook, it's a Flash! xD), lightweight, pretty, has physical buttons, and is simple. The only downside for me is that if you turn off the frontlight, it's quite dark, which wasn't the case with the PocketBook (or at least not that much), but it's a minor thing. You can still set the frontlight to 5%, and it's perfect.

During my hunt for the main colour e-reader, I came across a mini e-reader, and yeah, I hit the buy button. It was a bit impulsive, to be honest, but I am glad I did it. It's the XTEINK X4 Classic – no frontlight, no touch, just a small e-reader that I now carry everywhere.

I don't think it's life-changing because I need to get used to taking it out of my pocket instead of my phone, which is sometimes harder than you would think. But I hope I will get there. Anyway, below are a few pictures of all three devices.
